title: LMCache MP — Tiers (HBM / DRAM / NVMe)
description: Tier-aware LMCache MP observability. Replaces the legacy IP-mode HBM/DRAM dashboard, which targeted the lmcache:* namespace and renders empty under MP mode. Row 0 is run validity — if it is red, stop.

panels.title: Run validity — check this before reading anything else
Health
panels.description: Composite: 0 if the EventBus is dropping, l1_read_failure is moving, or L1 allocations are failing.

panels.title: EventBus dropped events
panels.description: MUST be 0. Non-zero means the bus tail-dropped at --event-bus-queue-size and every histogram on this dashboard is wrong.

panels.title: Post-lookup anomalies (l1_read_failure)
panels.description: MUST be 0. In MP mode reserve_read only runs after a successful lookup, so non-zero means a lookup/reserve race or unexpected eviction. Correctness problem, not performance.

panels.title: EventBus drain lag
panels.description: Seconds since the oldest queued event. Rising = drain thread falling behind.

panels.title: Token hit rate
panels.description: L1+L2 token-level hit rate. L0 (vLLM's own prefix cache) is excluded — it is not observable from LMCache.

panels.title: Outcome — what the user actually sees
TTFT (vLLM)
panels.description: The user-visible payoff. Every storage feature is ultimately claiming to move this.

panels.title: Token hit rate over time
panels.description: Should be roughly INVARIANT across storage-feature changes. If it moves between baseline and treatment, the workload changed and the comparison is void.

panels.title: GPU framebuffer used (DCGM)
panels.description: Actual HBM occupancy. Needed alongside l0_block_* because on the DGX under unified memory nvidia-smi does not report this reliably.

panels.title: GPU utilization
panels.description: Context for whether the GPU was actually the bottleneck.

panels.title: Chunks delivered to engine
panels.description: What the MP server hands back to each vLLM worker per retrieve().

panels.title: L0 block lifetime (HBM)
panels.description: Allocation to eviction, per sampled GPU block. SAMPLED — set --metrics-sample-rate 1.0 or this is noise.

panels.title: L0 block idle before evict
panels.description: Last access to eviction. Separates 'never reused' from 'evicted while still hot'.

panels.title: L0 block reuse gap
panels.description: Gap between consecutive accesses of the same GPU block.

panels.title: L1 occupancy
panels.description: Rising without plateau suggests a leak. Saturating at --l1-size-gb means the working set exceeds capacity.

panels.title: L1 usage ratio vs eviction watermark
panels.description: A demo run that never approaches the watermark is not exercising the tier and proves nothing about storage.

panels.title: Eviction loop: alive vs fired
panels.description: The loop polls at ~1 Hz. On a short benchmark it can tick without ever firing — that is why upstream exports both. Ticks with no fires means the run ended before the watermark was crossed.

panels.title: L1 chunk lifetime
panels.description: THE FDP METRIC. If this distribution is multimodal with N modes, that is the empirical case for N RUHs. If unimodal, more RUHs buy nothing and we should say so.

panels.title: Real reuse gap (time)
panels.description: Time between a chunk's last access and its next read — storage cost. Short gaps mean prefetch has little slack, which is what makes read prioritization matter.

panels.title: L2 occupancy by backend
panels.description: A missing series for an l2_name means either 'not configured' or 'get_usage() raised this scrape' — cross-check the store/load counters.

panels.title: L2 IOPS (fixed 1m window)
panels.description: Upstream exports no *_iops metric so dashboards pick their own window. Pinned to 1m in the recording rules so all three demos are comparable.

panels.title: L2 evictions
panels.description: Invalidation rate — the trim/deallocate traffic the device sees. Relevant to FDP reclaim behaviour.

panels.title: L1→L2 store throughput (submit→complete)
panels.description: PRIMARY for FDP and MDTS. Includes adapter queue, network and disk — this is bytes / end-to-end latency, not raw transfer rate. That is the right measure for MDTS (fewer commands is the benefit) but it means you cannot separate 'fewer commands' from 'faster device' here.

panels.title: L2→L1 load throughput (submit→complete)
panels.description: PRIMARY for read prioritization. Watch p99 against the store p99 — that gap is the read-under-write-pressure story.

panels.title: In-flight L2 stores vs loads
panels.description: THE CONTENTION SIGNAL. Sustained non-zero stores means the adapter cannot keep up with the L1→L2 write rate. The loads/stores balance is exactly what read prioritization is meant to shift.

panels.title: Active prefetch jobs
panels.description: Sustained high values indicate a slow L2 backend or polling delay. Should FALL with effective read prioritization.

panels.title: In-flight prefetch L1 reservation
panels.description: L1 bytes reserved by in-flight prefetch loads. Rising alongside L1 occupancy means prefetch reservations are crowding out cacheable data — a plausible way for prioritization to help one metric and hurt another.

panels.title: L0→L1 store throughput (GPU→CPU)
panels.description: CONTROL VARIABLE for the MDTS sweep. True GPU-stream copy time, unaffected by MDTS. If this moves between MDTS configurations, something other than MDTS changed and the comparison is invalid.

panels.title: L1→L0 load throughput (CPU→GPU)
panels.description: Same, load direction.

panels.title: Failure counters
panels.description: l1_allocation_failure = L1 OOM during reserve_write. l2_prefetch_failure{reason=l1_oom} = prefetch arrived but found no room — directly relevant to whether read prioritization is landing in time.

panels.title: EventBus health
panels.description: These observe bus state directly rather than being event-driven, so a failing subscriber cannot silence them. Proves the MEASUREMENT was clean, not just the workload.
